props.gloss_en: (entertained inference) our mishna implies: if the writer says 'give it', the found document is delivered -- even long after it was lost
Gittin 27a: an agent who lost a gett may use a found one only if found immediately
baraita: a woman's gett found in the market is returned to the wife when the husband admits it -- with no stated time limit
Rabba: the immediate-only rule holds where passing caravans are common; the return rule where they are not
refinement: even where caravans are common, the concern requires that two couples of identical names be established in one town
Rav Huna, on the gett found in his court naming Sheviri-on-the-Rakhis: we suspect a second town named Sheviri
mishna (20a): any court enactment that is found is returned -- Rabba's ground for returning the court gett
Rabba ruled in practice, per his own teaching, that the gett found at the Pumbedita flax-house be returned
version 1: it was found where flax is SOLD -- caravans frequent, but no two identical couples established
version 2: it was found where flax is SOAKED -- even with two identical couples established, since caravans are not frequent there
R' Zeira resolves the baraita against the Gittin mishna with the same caravans distinction
version A: R' Zeira withholds return only where the two couples are established -- identical to Rabba
version B: R' Zeira withholds return wherever caravans are common, even unestablished -- and disputes Rabba
(within the disputing version) Rabba reads 'court enactments are returned' as found IN court -- a caravan-like venue -- so only הוחזקו blocks return
(within the disputing version) R' Zeira reads it as found OUTSIDE court; found inside, it would not be returned
R' Yirmeya: the found gett is returned where its witnesses attest they never signed another gett for a man of that name
Rav Ashi: returned where the loser gives a clear-cut mark -- a hole beside such-and-such a letter; a bare 'it has a hole' is not enough
are ordinary distinguishing marks effective by Torah law or by rabbinic law? (Rav Ashi's unresolved doubt; hence he trusts only a clear-cut mark)
Rabba bar bar Chana's lost gett was returned to him after he offered both a mark and visual recognition
(entertained concern) the gett may have been written in Nisan and delivered in Tishrei, letting the wife unlawfully repossess produce sold in between
answer: when she comes to repossess, the court demands proof of when the gett reached her hand

why the same answer fails for promissory notes: a purchaser reads the court's returning of a NOTE as certifying its date, and will not demand proof; a gett he reads as returned only to free the wife to remarry
